text:
It sits outside my window

like an old woman going to market;

it sits and watches me,

sweats nervously

through wire and fog and dog-bark

until unexpectedly

I strike the screen with a newspaper

as if swatting a fly

and you could hear the scream

in this ordinary city,

and then it left.


the way to end a poem

like this

is to suddenly grow

silent.

translation.title: Love, Fame and Death
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the strange watcher outside the window and the self-conscious abrupt ending.
